title: Perf-canary: add fragmentation-induced tail latency scenario + release gating
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Goal
Add a dedicated perf-canary scenario that reliably reproduces fragmentation-induced p95/p99 latency inflation under bursty + mixed sequence-length traffic, and wire the checks into runtime release gating.

Why
We’ve repeatedly seen regressions where median stays flat but p99 spikes due to allocator churn / fragmentation. Unit + microbench tests don’t capture this. We need a stable canary to prevent shipping tail regressions, especially as we roll out compaction behind a flag.

Scope
1) New scenario in perf-canary that:
- Simulates bursty arrivals + mixed context lengths (prefill/decode interleaving)
- Exercises multi-tenant pool behavior (at least two priority classes) to ensure eviction/compaction doesn’t starve lower tier
- Runs long enough to reach a fragmented steady state (not just warmup)
- Captures KV fragmentation and allocator failure counters alongside latency

2) Release gating:
- Add the scenario to the runtime release pipeline (same tier as existing p99 canaries)
- Define pass/fail thresholds + rollback triggers (delta-based to handle cluster noise)
- Ensure artifacts (timeseries + logs) are retained and linked from the release run

References / context
- Postmortem: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/pm-2025-02-11-burst-tail-latency-kv-fragmentation.json
- Benchmark methodology: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/fragmentation-benchmarks-burst-tail-methodology.json
- Metrics naming: ENG-2842 + PR-18423 (fragmentation ratio / alloc failures)
- Perf scenario baseline work: ENG-2843 + benchmark-lab PR-912

Design (scenario definition)
Scenario name (proposed): kv_frag_burst_mix_v1
Workload model:
- Arrival pattern: bursts (e.g., 30s high QPS / 60s low QPS) for 20–30 minutes total
- Request mix:
  - 55% short context (0.5–2k), 35% medium (2–8k), 10% long (8–32k)
  - Decode lengths: mixture of 64/256/1024 tokens (weighted toward 256)
- Concurrency: fixed concurrency mode + optional adaptive mode (to mimic scheduler admission control)
- Tenants / priority classes:
  - Tier A (latency-sensitive) 70% traffic
  - Tier B (best-effort) 30% traffic
- Runtime flags:
  - Run matrix: compaction=off (baseline) and compaction=on (candidate), both with same batching limits
  - Use explicit budgets from ENG-2847 defaults (so we detect budget regressions)

Metrics to capture (must be in canary report)
Latency:
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, plus decode-only p99 if available
Allocator/fragmentation:
- kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio (gauge)
- kv_cache_alloc_fail_total (counter)
- kv_cache_evictions_total (counter)
- kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total (counter) [if compaction enabled]
- kv_cache_compaction_time_ms_total (counter) [or per-interval histo]
Quality/safety:
- Error rate / timeouts
- Any “fallback model/route” counts (to ensure we’re not masking performance by route changes)

Gating thresholds (initial proposal)
We want a guard that’s sensitive to tails but robust to noise:
- Hard fail if kv_cache_alloc_fail_total increases vs baseline run OR exceeds 0 (candidate should not introduce alloc failures in canary env).
- p99 regression gate (decode+e2e): candidate p99 must be <= baseline p99 * 1.05 (5% headroom) AND must not exceed an absolute ceiling specific to the pool (to be configured per canary environment).
- Fragmentation sanity: if fragmentation ratio is > 0.35 for >10% of the run window AND p99 is elevated, flag as failure. (We don’t fail solely on fragmentation ratio since it’s workload dependent, but it’s a strong signal when coupled with tails.)
- Compaction cost sanity (when enabled): compaction_time_ms_total per minute must remain within budget envelope (configured). Fail if compaction budget is exceeded for 3 consecutive intervals.

Acceptance criteria
- Scenario lands in perf-canary repo with clear parameters and a README section describing intent + typical failure modes.
- CI/release gating updated so runtime builds cannot progress if kv_frag_burst_mix_v1 fails.
- Canary output includes:
  - Latency summary (p50/p95/p99)
  - Fragmentation/alloc failure counters
  - Links to raw artifacts (timeseries + structured logs)
- Baseline run recorded for runtime-1.17 (or latest stable) and attached to this ticket.

Implementation plan
1) Implement scenario generator + request mix config (Rina)
2) Add metric collection wiring for new KV metrics (coordinate with Logan/Caleb if schema gaps appear)
3) Add gating rule in release pipeline (Connor + Kira for LTS stability)
4) Run baselines in at least two environments:
   - Hosted canary region (standard GPU pool)
   - One Dedicated-like pool (if available in canary infra)
5) Tune thresholds based on baseline variance across 3 runs

Risks / mitigations
- Flakiness due to shared cluster noise: mitigate via delta-based gates + running baseline and candidate on same canary cluster back-to-back.
- Scenario too slow (release pipeline time): keep run length to <=30 minutes and allow a shorter “smoke” variant for PR-level checks; full gate on release train only.
- Masked regressions via route changes: explicitly pin model + disable fallback routing in canary config where possible.

Links
- perf-canary PR (in progress): sources/github/perf-canary/pr-388.json
- benchmark-lab PR for workload definition: sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-912.json

Updates
2025-02-21 (Rina Kobayashi)
- Drafted kv_frag_burst_mix_v1 config based on the fragmentation bench methodology. Added tenant split + burst phases. Need confirmation from Sofia/Julian on whether canary harness can emit scheduler cache-pressure events as annotations.

2025-02-25 (Marcus Reed)
- Ran the scenario locally against runtime-1.17 (compaction off). Able to reproduce allocator churn and ~18–25% p99 inflation vs steady load after ~12 minutes. Good signal; need to verify we’re not saturating GPU due to an unrelated batching change.

2025-02-28 (Sean Gallagher)
- From SRE perspective: please add an explicit hard gate on alloc failures. Any non-zero alloc failures in canary should fail release. Also ensure artifacts are retained for 14d and linked from the release run.

2025-03-03 (Kira Volkov)
- Added release gating hook (draft). Suggest: run baseline (last-good) nightly, and candidate on release; gate on regression vs last-good to reduce noise. Need decision on whether last-good is pinned to runtime-1.17.x or tracks main.

Open questions
- Should last-good baseline track the latest green on main, or the last shipped runtime tag? (Preference: last shipped tag for stability; but it may lag improvements and create false positives.)
- Do we want a second scenario focused on long-context OOM risk (KV pressure) or keep that as separate canary?

Next steps
- Get sign-off on thresholds from Marcus + Sean + Allison (alerts alignment)
- Merge perf-canary PR and validate in release train dry-run
- Record baseline artifacts and attach links here before moving to Done
